column1: # levels.tsv --- THE INK LEVELS for pencil-your-own. Yours to edit; that is the point.
# Borrowed verbatim in vocabulary from c4/h/m0ve-ink.tsv (Corwin's ruling, 2026-08-29), because a
# second scale for the same idea would be a new fact about the world minted by me -- exactly the
# thing this skill says not to ink. If m0ve's table moves, move this one to match and say so.
# THE RULE, one line, and pencil.sh prints it too:
#     a concern of ink k gates while reality r >= 1 - k.
# Fully inked (1.0) gates at every reality -- it is a fact about the world, not a choice.
# An uninked line (0.0) gates only under a full reality check.
# FILE BY WORDS. A concern row carries the NAME, never the LEVEL. `pencil` is one bare word;
# `0.5` is a literal whose meaning rides on a typographic point, and the shop's law is that the
# separator is never typography. pencil.sh REFUSES a numeric literal and tells you which word
# you meant.
# WHY THIS IS A FILE AND NOT A REGEX INSIDE THE TOOL: if I picked the scale inside the
# instrument I would be committing the fault the instrument measures. Strike a row and a level
# disappears. Add one and it appears. Neither needs my agreement.
# name: the one bare word a concern row cites.
# level: the ink, in [0,1]. The gating stop 1-level is derived; do not write it.
# means: what claiming this level asserts about the concern.
name
inked
column3: a fact about the world, with a witness that is not me. Gates even in the dream.

column1: firm
column3: established here, and I would defend it. Drops only when you are frankly dreaming.

column1: pencil
column3: a working assumption I am willing to name as one. Drops at half reality.

column1: faint
column3: a guess kept visible on purpose. Drops early; the losers stay in the drawing.

column1: uninked
column3: a line I drew and do not stand behind. Gates only under a full reality check.
